doc.title: Nancy Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995

title: Advice to a young singer
summary: She tells young singers to sing anywhere, work small rooms and learn their craft before people.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: Well, this has really been fascinating.
And do you have anything to say to a young singer in Columbus, Ohio trying to get to New York?

Sing anyplace they ask you to sing. Use your voice. Work. Learn your craft. And you can’t learn your craft at home. You need to work those little rooms. You need to put your music in front of people, not in a studio. You need to work. And this is something they’ve gotten away from. And we need rooms for these young people to learn their craft. We need more little Club Regals and more little places for kids to play. More places where you can just go and just have a piano if you can’t have a rhythm section. The object of the game is to put your music and put yourself in front of people. You don’t learn your craft just in front of a microphone.
